senses.en: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell

examples.text: The dictator's diabolical regime tortured dissidents and starved entire provinces into submission.

senses.en: showing the cunning or ingenuity or wickedness typical of a devil

examples.text: The villain devised a diabolical scheme that fooled even the most seasoned detectives.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diábolos(악마)에서 왔고 '이간질하며 중상하는 자'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An ornamental headband worn as a badge of royalty.

examples.text: The Apollon wing of the Louvre has a set of historic crowns, diadems and sovereign jewellery.

senses.en: Regal power; sovereignty; empire—considered as symbolized by the crown.

examples.text: The young prince was too eager to inherit the diadem and the burdens that came with it.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diádēma(머리에 두르는 띠)에서 왔고 diadéō(둘러 묶다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: so thin as to transmit light

examples.text: The bride's diaphanous veil floated in the breeze, barely hiding her face.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diaphanḗs '투과해 보이는'에서 왔습니다. 빛이 통과해 비치는 얇은 천의 이미지입니다.

senses.en: An abusive, bitter verbal or written attack, criticism or denunciation.

examples.text: The senator was prone to diatribes which could go on for more than an hour.

origin.ko: 그리스어 diatribḗ(시간을 보냄, 강론)에서 왔습니다. 닳도록 오래 이어지는 연설이 '통렬한 비난'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: being twofold; a classification into two opposed parts or subclasses

examples.text: the dichotomy between eastern and western culture

origin.ko: 그리스어 dikhotomía에서 왔습니다. 둘로 자른다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To order, command, control.

examples.text: Etiquette dictates that wedding invitations should be acknowledged in writing.

senses.en: a guiding principle

examples.text: the dictates of reason

origin.ko: 라틴어 dictō(되풀이해 말하다)에서 왔습니다. 말로 불러주는 데서 '명령하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: expecting unquestioning obedience

examples.text: The manager's dictatorial style left no room for questions or dissent among his staff.

senses.en: characteristic of an absolute ruler or absolute rule; having absolute sovereignty

examples.text: The dictatorial ruler silenced the press and jailed every opponent who questioned his decrees.

senses.en: an authoritative declaration

examples.text: The coach's dictum that practice makes perfect shaped how the whole team trained.

senses.en: A judicial opinion expressed by judges on points that do not necessarily arise in the case, and are not involved in it.

examples.text: The judge's dictum on press freedom was not binding but was widely quoted in later cases.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dictum(말해진 것, 격언)에서 왔고 dīcō(말하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Excessively moralizing.

examples.text: The novel's didactic tone made readers feel they were being lectured rather than entertained.

senses.en: Instructive or intended to teach or demonstrate, especially with regard to morality.

examples.text: didactic poetry

origin.ko: 그리스어 didaktikós(가르치는 데 능한)에서 왔고 didáskō(가르치다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To recognize as different or distinct.

examples.text: How do you differentiate a fake smile from a genuine one?

senses.en: To show or be the difference or distinction between things.

examples.text: What differentiates an alligator from a crocodile?

senses.en: become different during development

examples.text: cells differentiate

origin.ko: 라틴어 differentia(차이)에서 왔고 difference에서 파생한 말입니다.

senses.en: lack of self-confidence

examples.text: Her diffidence kept her from speaking up, even when she knew the answer.

origin.ko: 라틴어 diffīdere(믿지 못하다)에서 왔습니다. 처음엔 남을 불신한다는 뜻이었고, 1650년대에 '자신을 못 믿는' 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking self-confidence

examples.text: stood in the doorway diffident and abashed

senses.en: showing modest reserve

examples.text: she was diffident when offering a comment on the professor's lecture

origin.ko: 라틴어 diffīdere(믿지 못하다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: lacking conciseness

examples.text: a diffuse historical novel

senses.en: To spread (something) over or through as in air, water, or other matter, especially by fluid motion or passive means.

examples.text: Ideas are easily diffused with the help of technology.

senses.en: spread out; not concentrated in one place

examples.text: a large diffuse organization

origin.ko: 라틴어 diffundere(사방으로 쏟다)에서 왔습니다. 퍼져 흩어져서 '장황한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lose clarity or turn aside especially from the main subject of attention or course of argument in writing, thinking, or speaking

examples.text: She always digresses when telling a story

origin.ko: 라틴어 digredi(따로 걸어가다)에서 왔습니다. 본래 길에서 옆으로 빠지는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: An aside, an act of straying from the main subject in speech or writing.

examples.text: The lectures included lengthy digressions on topics ranging from the professor's dog to the meaning of life.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīgressiō에서 왔습니다. 주제에서 옆으로 걸어 나간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Having fallen into a state of disrepair or deterioration, especially through neglect.

examples.text: The dilapidated farmhouse had sagging beams and windows that had not been repaired in decades.

senses.en: To become wider or larger; to expand.

examples.text: The eye doctor put drops in my eye to dilate the pupil so he could see the nerve better.

senses.en: add details, as to an account or idea; clarify the meaning of and discourse in a learned way, usually in writing

examples.text: The author declined to dilate on her methods, saying the appendix covered them thoroughly enough.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīlātāre(넓게 펼치다)에서 왔고 lātus(넓은)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: Slow or tardy.

examples.text: The dilatory contractor missed every deadline and left the renovation unfinished for months.

senses.en: Intentionally delaying (someone or something), intended to cause delay, gain time, or adjourn decision.

examples.text: a dilatory strategy

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīlātōrius(미루는)에서 왔고 differō에서 나왔습니다. delay와는 어원이 다릅니다.

senses.en: an amateur who engages in an activity without serious intentions and who pretends to have knowledge

examples.text: The dilettante sampled painting, pottery and poetry but never mastered any of them.

senses.en: showing frivolous or superficial interest; amateurish

examples.text: his dilettantish efforts at painting

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 dilettare(즐기다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 즐기기 위해 하는 아마추어를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks

examples.text: a diligent search of the files

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīligō(아끼다, 문자대로 '골라내다')에서 왔습니다. 골라 아끼는 마음으로 정성을 들이는 모습입니다.

senses.en: very small

examples.text: diminutive in stature

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīminuere(줄이다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: a loud harsh or strident noise

examples.text: The din of the construction site made conversation across the street nearly impossible.

senses.en: instill (into a person) by constant repetition

examples.text: he dinned the lessons into his students

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dyne(소음)에서 왔고 인도유럽어 어근 '소리 내다'로 거슬러 올라갑니다.

senses.en: Shabby, squalid, uncared-for.

examples.text: The dingy apartment smelled of damp and its walls were stained from years of neglect.

senses.en: Dark, dull.

examples.text: The dingy light of a winter afternoon made the office feel even more oppressive.

origin.ko: 켄트 방언 dingy(더러운)에서 왔다고 보며, 확실하지 않습니다. dung(똥)에서 왔을 가능성이 있습니다.

senses.en: interchangeable with ‘means’ in the expression ‘by means of’

examples.text: By dint of sheer persistence, she finished the marathon despite a severe injury.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 dynt(타격, 일격)에서 왔습니다. 일격으로 이뤄낸 힘에서 'by dint of'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: A mournful poem or piece of music composed or performed as a memorial to a deceased person.

examples.text: It was as if the night sang dirges with clenched teeth.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dirige(인도하소서)에서 왔습니다. 장례 기도문의 첫머리 말이 그대로 '장송곡'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To free (someone) of a misconception or misapprehension; to unveil a falsehood held by (someone).

examples.text: If we had any hopes or illusions about the National Party before they came into office, we were disabused of them quickly.

origin.ko: dis-와 abuse를 합친 말로, 프랑스어 désabuser와 비교됩니다. 속은 것을 풀어 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: discontented as toward authority

examples.text: Disaffected voters stayed home, convinced that neither party would address their concerns.

senses.en: An act or expression of condemnation or disapproval, especially on moral grounds.

examples.text: The council's disapprobation of the plan was evident in the stony silence that followed.

senses.en: To perceive, recognize, or comprehend with the mind; to descry.

examples.text: Critics could discern a hint of irony beneath the author's earnest prose.

senses.en: To distinguish something as being different from something else; to differentiate or discriminate.

examples.text: He was too young to discern right from wrong.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discernere(갈라 구별하다)에서 왔습니다. 체로 걸러 따로 나누는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: perceptible by the senses or intellect

examples.text: the newspaper reports no discernible progress in the negotiations

origin.ko: discern에 -ible이 붙은 말로, 가려낼 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having or revealing keen insight and good judgment

examples.text: a discerning critic

senses.en: To embarrass (someone) greatly; to confuse; to perplex; to disconcert.

examples.text: The reporter's blunt question visibly discomfited the minister, who fumbled for an answer.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desconfit(패배한)에서 왔습니다. 원래 '무너뜨리다'였고 discomfort와 혼동되어 '당황시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To upset the composure of; to startle.

examples.text: The embrace disconcerted the daughter-in-law somewhat, as the caresses of old gentlemen unshorn and perfumed with tobacco might well do.

senses.en: To frustrate, discomfit.

examples.text: The emperor disconcerted the plans of his enemy.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 desconcerter에서 왔습니다. 맞춰진 조화를 흩뜨려 당황하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: sad beyond comforting; incapable of being consoled
senses.ko: 위로할 수 없을 만큼 슬픈, 실의에 빠진

examples.text: For weeks after the death of her cat she was disconsolate.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 discōnsōlātus(위로받지 못한)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: lack of agreement or harmony

examples.text: Discord among the coalition partners threatened to bring down the government before the budget vote.

senses.en: a harsh mixture of sounds

examples.text: The untuned instruments produced a painful discord that made the audience wince.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discors(마음이 갈라진)에서 왔습니다. 마음(cor)이 따로따로이니 '불화'입니다.

senses.en: not in agreement or harmony

examples.text: views discordant with present-day ideas

senses.en: lacking in harmony

examples.text: The discordant notes of the out-of-tune piano echoed through the empty hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discordāre(마음이 안 맞다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: To disregard or regard as unimportant.

examples.text: Owing to his reputation, they discounted his comments.

senses.en: A reduction in price.

examples.text: For the summer sale, there was 40% discount in all the stores at the mall.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 discomputō(차감하다)에서 왔습니다. 셈에서 덜어내는 데서 '대수롭지 않게 보다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To cause (an idea or piece of evidence) to seem false or unreliable.

examples.text: The evidence would tend to discredit such a theory.

senses.en: damage the reputation of

examples.text: This newspaper story discredits the politicians

origin.ko: dis-와 credit(신용)을 합친 말입니다. 믿음을 없앤다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by prudence or modesty and wise self-restraint

examples.text: his trusted discreet aide

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrētus(가려낸)에서 왔습니다. 옳고 그름을 가려내는 분별에서 '신중한'이 되었습니다. discrete와 이중어입니다.

senses.en: An inconsistency between facts or sentiments.

examples.text: They found a discrepancy between the first set of test results and the second, and they're still trying to figure out why.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrepantia에서 왔고 discrepō(소리가 어긋나다)가 뿌리입니다. 소리가 맞지 않는 데서 '불일치'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: constituting a separate entity or part

examples.text: a government with three discrete divisions

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrētus(갈라진)에서 왔습니다. discreet와 이중어입니다.

senses.en: having or using the ability to act or decide according to your own discretion or judgment

examples.text: The commission has discretionary power to award extra funds

origin.ko: discretion(분별, 재량)에 -ary가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: To make distinctions.

examples.text: Since he was color blind he was unable to discriminate between the blue and green bottles.

senses.en: To make decisions harmful to (a person or group) based on prejudice.

examples.text: The law prohibits discriminating against people based on their skin color.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discrīmināre(갈라 구별하다)에서 왔고 discernō(가려내다)와 이어집니다.

senses.en: showing or indicating careful judgment and discernment especially in matters of taste

examples.text: The restaurant attracts discriminating customers who expect high-quality ingredients.

senses.en: (of e.g. speech and writing) tending to depart from the main point or cover a wide range of subjects

examples.text: a rambling discursive book

senses.en: proceeding to a conclusion by reason or argument rather than intuition

examples.text: Philosophy proceeds by discursive reasoning rather than by flashes of intuition or revelation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 discursus(이리저리 달림)에서 왔습니다. 이야기가 이곳저곳으로 뛰어다니는 모습입니다.

senses.en: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike

examples.text: The cat viewed the cheap supermarket catfood with disdain and stalked away.

senses.en: reject with contempt

examples.text: The critic disdained popular fiction, refusing even to review novels he considered beneath serious attention.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desdeignier(가치 없다고 여기다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: go ashore

examples.text: The passengers disembarked at Southampton

senses.en: deprive of voting rights

examples.text: Strict identification laws could disenfranchise elderly voters who no longer hold a valid driver's license.

senses.en: free from involvement or entanglement

examples.text: How can I disentangle myself from her personal affairs?

senses.en: To unravel; to separate into discrete components or units.

examples.text: This overlapping is reflective of hybrid languages, where certain features (phonetic, orthographic, semantic, syntactic) are also difficult to disentangle.

senses.en: To vomit or spew, to discharge.

examples.text: The train disgorged hundreds of commuters onto the crowded platform.

senses.en: To surrender (stolen goods or money, for example) unwillingly.

examples.text: Regulators forced the firm to disgorge the profits it had made through insider trading.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 desgorger에서 왔습니다. 목구멍(gorge)에서 쏟아낸다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: made less hopeful or enthusiastic

examples.text: felt discouraged by the magnitude of the problem

origin.ko: 동사 hearten(용기를 북돋우다)에서 온 말입니다. 용기를 잃은 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: To free or deprive of illusion; to disenchant.
senses.ko: 환상에서 깨어나게 하다, 환멸을 느끼게 하다

examples.text: Years of bureaucratic delay began to disillusion the once-idealistic young volunteers.

origin.ko: dis-와 illusion을 합친 말로, 환상을 걷어낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not straightforward or candid; giving a false appearance of frankness

examples.text: a disingenuous excuse

senses.en: Having no interest or stake in the outcome, and no conflicts of interest; free of bias, impartial.

examples.text: A disinterested mediator with no stake in the dispute is needed to settle the contract.

senses.en: Synonym of uninterested (“not interested; not concerned; indifferent”).

examples.text: Robin took to wandering again, to intermittent travel from which she came back hours, days later, disinterested.

origin.ko: dis-와 interested를 합친 말이거나 disinterest의 과거분사로 봅니다. 이해관계가 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking orderly continuity

examples.text: The witness gave a disjointed account that jumped between events without clear order.

senses.en: bar from attention or consideration

examples.text: She dismissed the idea as ridiculous.

senses.en: terminate the employment of; discharge from an office or position

examples.text: The company dismissed me after less than a year.

senses.en: cease to consider; put out of judicial consideration

examples.text: The court dismissed the case.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīmittō(보내 버리다)에서 왔습니다. 멀리 내보내는 이미지가 '묵살하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: express a negative opinion of

examples.text: She disparaged her student's efforts

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desparagier(신분이 맞지 않게 하다)에서 왔습니다. 동등한 지위(parage)에서 끌어내린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: fundamentally different or distinct in quality or kind

examples.text: such disparate attractions as grand opera and game fishing

origin.ko: 라틴어 disparātus(갈라 놓은)에서 왔습니다. 서로 나뉘어 이질적이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unaffected by strong emotion or prejudice

examples.text: a journalist should be a dispassionate reporter of fact

senses.en: the property of being prompt and efficient

examples.text: We must act with dispatch in this matter.

senses.en: dispose of rapidly and without delay and efficiently

examples.text: He dispatched the task he was assigned

senses.en: send away towards a designated goal

examples.text: Scores of foreign journalists have been dispatched to Seoul to report on the growing tensions between the two Koreas and the possibility of war.

origin.ko: 스페인어 despachar나 이탈리아어 dispacciare에서 왔다고 보며, 자세한 기원은 불확실합니다.

senses.en: an exemption from some rule or obligation

examples.text: The school granted her a special dispensation to submit the thesis after the usual deadline.

senses.en: the act of dispensing (giving out in portions)

examples.text: a fair dispensation of money

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispēnsātiō에서 왔습니다. 저울에 달아 나누어 주는 데서 '면제, 특별 허가'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: administer or bestow, as in small portions

examples.text: He is delighted to dispense a share of it to all the company.

senses.en: grant a dispensation; grant an exemption

examples.text: I was dispensed from this terrible task

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispendere(달아서 나누다)에서 왔습니다. 무게를 달아 조금씩 나누어 준다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: move away from each other

examples.text: The crowds dispersed

senses.en: to cause to separate and go in different directions

examples.text: Police used loudspeakers to disperse the protesters before the evening curfew began.

senses.en: To disseminate.

examples.text: Volunteers helped disperse leaflets about the new vaccination program across the rural district.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispergō(흩뿌리다)에서 왔고 spargō(뿌리다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: To amuse oneself divertingly or playfully; in particular, to cavort or gambol.

examples.text: Children disported themselves in the shallow surf while their parents dozed on the sand.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desporter(즐겁게 놀다)에서 왔습니다. 일에서 몸을 옮겨 놀이하는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: Temperament, temperamental makeup or habitual mood.

examples.text: She has a sunny disposition.

senses.en: an attitude of mind especially one that favors one alternative over others

examples.text: Salt has a disposition to dissolve in water.

senses.en: Final decision or settlement.

examples.text: The disposition of the case will be announced tomorrow.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dispositiō(배치)에서 왔습니다. 마음이 놓인 상태가 '기질'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: causing mental discomfort

examples.text: the disquieting sounds of nearby gunfire

senses.en: A lengthy, formal discourse that analyses or explains some topic; (loosely) a dissertation or treatise.

examples.text: The professor's disquisition on medieval trade routes ran well past the end of the seminar.

origin.ko: 라틴어 disquīsītiō(탐구)에서 왔고 disquīrō(샅샅이 조사하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: hide under a false appearance

examples.text: He masked his disappointment

senses.en: make believe with the intent to deceive

examples.text: He dissembled sleep so that the guards would not question him during the long night.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 dissembler에서 왔고 라틴어 dissimulō(숨기다)에 기원합니다. 겉모습을 다르게 꾸민다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who professes beliefs and opinions that he or she does not hold in order to conceal his or her real feelings or motives

examples.text: The senator proved a skilled dissembler, smiling warmly at rivals he was quietly working to undermine.

origin.ko: dissemble에 -er이 붙어 본심을 숨기는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: cause to become widely known

examples.text: The values of the human rights movement have disseminated throughout the world.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissēmināre(씨를 흩뿌리다)에서 왔습니다. 씨 뿌리듯 널리 퍼뜨린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: be of different opinions

examples.text: Several Republicans dissented

senses.en: Disagreement with the ideas, doctrines, decrees, etc. of a political party, government or religion.

examples.text: A system that suppresses dissent is fault-intolerant, ignorant and fragile.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissentīre(다르게 느끼다)에서 왔습니다. 생각이 서로 달라 '반대하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person who dissents from some established policy

examples.text: The exiled dissident continued to publish essays criticizing the government from abroad.

senses.en: disagreeing, especially with a majority

examples.text: The dissident faction within the party voted against the leadership's proposal.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissideō(떨어져 앉다)에서 왔습니다. 다수와 따로 앉은 사람이 '반체제 인사'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: hide (feelings) from other people

examples.text: He dissimulated his anger behind a polite smile throughout the tense negotiation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissimulō(숨기다, 가장하다)에서 왔고 dissimilis(닮지 않은)에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: spend frivolously and unwisely

examples.text: The heir dissipated his inheritance on gambling and lavish parties within a few short years.

senses.en: move away from each other

examples.text: By noon the morning fog had dissipated and the valley was bright with sunlight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissipō(흩어버리다)에서 왔습니다. 흩뿌려 없애는 데서 '탕진하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: separation into component parts

examples.text: The dissolution of the empire left dozens of newly independent states in its wake.

senses.en: The termination of an organized body or legislative assembly, especially a formal dismissal.

examples.text: The dissolution of parliament triggered a snap election within six weeks.

senses.en: The quality of being dissolute.

examples.text: He led a life of dissolution, drinking and gambling almost daily.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissolūtiō(풀어 해체함)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a conflict of people's opinions or actions or characters

examples.text: Cognitive dissonance exists when a person possesses two cognitions, one of which is contradictory to the other

senses.en: A harsh, discordant combination of sounds.

examples.text: The orchestra's deliberate dissonance unsettled listeners accustomed to more melodic compositions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dissonantia에서 왔습니다. 소리가 어울리지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characteristic of or peculiar to a woman

examples.text: They inherit Plantagenet blood by direct descent, and Tudor on the distaff side.

senses.en: the sphere of work by women

examples.text: Historians once treated the distaff as a footnote, though women's labor sustained the household economy.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 distæf에서 왔고 '아마 다발'과 stæf(막대)의 합성입니다. 실 잣는 일이 여자의 몫이라 '여성의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: swell from or as if from internal pressure

examples.text: The distended bellies of the starving cows

senses.en: cause to expand as if by internal pressure

examples.text: The gas distended the animal's body

senses.en: extract by the process of distillation

examples.text: The editor distilled a sprawling report into a one-page summary of its central findings.

senses.en: remove impurities from, increase the concentration of, and separate through the process of distillation

examples.text: The plant distills seawater to produce drinking water for the island's residents.

senses.en: a distinguishing difference between similar things or people

examples.text: There is a distinction to be made between resting and slacking.

senses.en: an honor awarded to someone in recognition of achievement or superiority

examples.text: She had the distinction of meeting the Queen.

origin.ko: 라틴어 distinctiō(구별)에서 왔고 distinguō(구분하다)의 명사형입니다.

senses.en: make false by mutilation or addition; as of a message or story

examples.text: In their articles, journalists sometimes distort the truth.

senses.en: twist and press out of shape

examples.text: The old glass distorted the reflection, stretching faces into strange, wavering shapes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 distorquēre(비틀다)에서 왔습니다. 비틀어 모양을 일그러뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: afflicted with or marked by anxious uneasiness or trouble or grief

examples.text: She is distressed because she can't find her keys.

senses.en: facing or experiencing financial trouble or difficulty

examples.text: distressed companies need loans and technical advice

senses.en: act nervously; be undecided; be uncertain

examples.text: While the committee dithered over the budget, the deadline for funding quietly passed.

senses.en: an excited state of agitation

examples.text: he was in a dither

origin.ko: 중세 영어 dideren(떨다)에서 온 didder의 변형입니다. 떨듯 우물쭈물한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: of or belonging to or active during the day

examples.text: Most birds are diurnal.

senses.en: having a daily cycle or occurring every day

examples.text: diurnal rotation of the heavens

origin.ko: 라틴어 diurnālis에서 왔고 diēs(날)가 뿌리입니다. journal과 이중어입니다.

senses.en: extend in a different direction

examples.text: Their interests diverged

senses.en: be at variance with; be out of line with

examples.text: The software is pretty good, except for a few cases where its behavior diverges from user expectations.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 dīvergō(다른 쪽으로 꺾다)에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: diverging from another or from a standard

examples.text: a divergent opinion

senses.en: tending to move apart in different directions

examples.text: The two research teams followed divergent paths and reached very different conclusions about the data.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dis-와 vergere(향하다)에 -ent가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: having variety of character or form or components; or having increased variety

examples.text: diversified farming

senses.en: turn aside; turn away from

examples.text: The workers diverted the stream away from the road.

senses.en: occupy in an agreeable, entertaining or pleasant fashion

examples.text: Street musicians diverted the waiting passengers during the long delay at the station.

senses.en: withdraw (money) and move into a different location, often secretly and with dishonest intentions

examples.text: Investigators found that the manager had diverted charity funds into his own personal accounts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 divertere(갈라져 돌아서다)에서 왔습니다. 방향을 돌린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: take away possessions from someone

examples.text: He was divested of his rights and his title

senses.en: reduce or dispose of; cease to hold (an investment)

examples.text: Glasgow will become the first university in Europe to divest from fossil fuels.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 desvestir(옷을 벗기다)에서 왔습니다. 옷을 벗기듯 소유물을 빼앗는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: perceive intuitively or through some inexplicable perceptive powers

examples.text: She could divine her employer's mood from the way he closed the office door.

senses.en: emanating from God

examples.text: divine guidance

senses.en: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods

examples.text: her pies were simply divine

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīvīnus(신의)에서 왔고 divus(신)가 뿌리입니다. 신의 영감으로 알아챈다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Cut off, or separated.

examples.text: divorced from reality

senses.en: of someone whose marriage has been legally dissolved

examples.text: Mark's parents are divorced.

senses.en: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret

examples.text: I will never divulge that secret to anyone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 dīvulgō(널리 알리다)에서 왔고 vulgus(대중)가 뿌리입니다.
